title: Axon/Fusus ALPR platform-control baseline for Syracuse comparison
summary: Current primary Axon documentation defines distinct search, retention, hotlist, permission, sharing, export and audit controls. This establishes a testable platform-control matrix for Syracuse, while the actual Syracuse configuration remains unresolved beyond the already-landed city policy/procurement/deployment baseline.

sources.title: Axon Fusus ALPR Sharing product guide
Axon Fusus ALPR Search product guide
Axon Fusus ALPR Administration product guide
Axon Fusus ALPR Audit product guide

caveats: Axon documentation describes product capabilities and defaults, not Syracuse's production configuration.
Fusus can surface third-party sources including Flock V3; Fusus presence does not identify reader ownership or prove a migrated Flock feed.

Axon's ALPR Data Sharing audit currently warns that Device Scope and Data Conditions can display generic values that do not reflect live sharing conditions; Sharing Management is needed to verify configured relationships.
Axon notes that some audit fields for roughly pre-April-2026 activity may be blank or incomplete because the legacy audit system did not capture all current fields.
No user, partner, hotlist, reader, source feed, sharing edge, or migration edge is inferred for Syracuse from vendor documentation.

methods: open-PR ownership and exact-head gate review
reuse of landed Syracuse #1903 canonical records

data.question: What Axon/Fusus ALPR control surfaces must be verified natively to distinguish product capability from Syracuse's deployed configuration and from the former Flock state?
data.method: Reconciled current Axon ALPR Sharing, Search, Administration and Audit guides with the already-canonical Syracuse #1903 policy, procurement and activation records without promoting vendor capabilities into Syracuse-specific facts.
data.framework: source/device ownership → retention → search requirements → hotlists/alerts → user/admin permissions → sharing conditions → export boundaries → audit evidence; Flock closeout and any migration remain separate predicates.
data.scope: Public platform and municipal-policy evidence only; no private-person enrichment.
findings: Axon separates read retention from hit retention and gates search, hotlist management and system administration with distinct role permissions; ALPR System Administration controls retention/alert settings and access to audit/sharing administration.

Axon ALPR Search records offense category and reason, allows case number to be hidden, optional or required by administrators, and can query multiple source classes including Axon devices and third-party feeds such as Flock V3.

Cross-agency ALPR Sharing is donor-initiated, requires recipient acceptance, can be revoked by either side, keeps donor data in the donor tenant, and applies donor-controlled offense-category eligibility to partner searches.

Shared partner detections can be queried in place; bulk CSV and bulk PDF exports exclude shared detections, while an individual detection PDF may include a shared record labeled with the originating agency.

Axon exposes Internal ALPR Activity, Network ALPR Activity, ALPR Data Sharing, and ALPR Hotlist Management audit reports; reports can cover historical periods in 31-day windows, but some pre-April-2026 legacy fields may be incomplete.

The ALPR Data Sharing audit has a documented condition-summary limitation: Device Scope and Data Conditions can show generic All Devices / Full Sharing values regardless of actual invite settings, so live Sharing Management relationship details outrank those summary columns.
Axon's Transparency Portal can disclose partner agencies with access to shared ALPR data, creating a public cross-check against native Sharing Management and audit exports.

For Syracuse, the landed municipal policy/procurement/deployment evidence remains configuration evidence only where it is explicit: vendor documentation does not establish current Syracuse partner relationships, configured retention values, source mix, users/roles, hotlists, case-number setting, or migration from Flock.
conclusions: Issue #2100 now has a canonical platform-control baseline that can be joined to native Syracuse records without conflating Flock and Axon/Fusus.

The next Syracuse evidence package should capture current ALPR Settings, Roles & Permissions, LPR Search Settings, source/device inventory, Sharing Management, Transparency Portal disclosure, and the four audit report families, then reconcile them against SPD Policy 427 and the 26-reader rollout.

Any claim that Flock-era data, users, hotlists, cases, or sharing relationships migrated into Axon requires a separate migration artifact; absence of such a record remains unresolved rather than assumed.
recommendations: Recover Syracuse screenshots/exports or native records for ALPR Settings, LPR Search Settings, role assignments, source inventory and Sharing Management.
Export current Internal ALPR Activity, Network ALPR Activity, ALPR Data Sharing and Hotlist Management reports for bounded date windows and preserve known report limitations.
Compare the public Axon Transparency Portal sharing disclosure with live Sharing Management and audit history.
Join current source/device identifiers to the 26-reader procurement/deployment records and separately test whether any Flock V3 or other third-party feed remains connected.
Keep Flock closeout and any migration of users, hotlists, cases, reads or historical exports as explicit unresolved edges until native evidence exists.
counterarguments: Vendor documentation can change and may describe capabilities not enabled in a given tenant; only Syracuse-native configuration and audit records establish deployed state.

A public transparency portal may omit details needed to reconstruct effective dates or conditions, so it should be treated as a public disclosure surface rather than the canonical sharing configuration.
The presence of a Flock V3 source option in Axon does not imply Syracuse uses it.
limitations: No Syracuse tenant export, Sharing Management view, ALPR Settings snapshot, user-role export, hotlist export, audit export, current source inventory, or migration record was recovered in this pass.
unresolved: What are Syracuse's live read/hit retention values and case-number/search settings?
Which users and roles have read/hit, hotlist, and ALPR system-administration permissions?
Which source/device types are active across all 26 planned readers and any third-party feeds?
Which partner sharing relationships are active, with what conditions and effective dates?
What do current audit exports and the Transparency Portal show, and do they agree with Sharing Management?
Did any Flock-era data, users, hotlists, cases, credentials or sharing state migrate into Axon/Fusus?

data.research_question: Can the already-researched Axon/Fusus capability findings be promoted into a canonical, source-grounded control matrix without inventing Syracuse-specific configuration or Flock-to-Axon continuity?
data.method: After open-PR work was sibling-owned/in progress and the seeded AI-lab transaction remained claimed by Worker 1, selected modulo-4 issue #2100, deduped the repo and issue history, refreshed current primary Axon documentation, and joined those capabilities to existing Syracuse #1903 records.
classification_rules: Vendor product capability is not treated as Syracuse configured state.
Fusus is not equivalent to an Axon-owned reader; source/device identity remains explicit.
Historical 26-site planning and the later 26-reader agreement do not establish a current one-to-one site inventory.
Sharing audit summary fields do not override live Sharing Management when Axon documents a summary limitation.
Shared search access is not modeled as data replication.
No Flock-to-Axon migration edge is created without native evidence.

findings.finding: Current primary Axon docs support a concrete eight-part control matrix for capture/source, search, hotlists, retention, roles, sharing, export boundaries and auditability.
Syracuse-native configured values and transition/migration state remain unresolved beyond already-landed municipal policy/procurement/deployment records.
